knowledge:
- key_parameters: genes=A named binary vector where 1 indicates differentially expressed (DE) and 0 indicates not DE, with names as unique gene identifiers ;; genome=UCSC genome identifier string (e.g., "hg19") ;; id=Gene identifier format string (e.g., "ensGene", "knownGene", "geneSymbol") ;; bias.data=Numeric vector containing the numeric value of the DE bias to account for (e.g., gene length or read counts) if not using native database values ;; method=Testing method to use: "Wallenius" (default approximation), "Sampling" (random sampling), or "Hypergeometric" (no bias correction) ;; repcnt=Integer specifying the number of random samples to generate when method="Sampling" ;; test.cats=Vector specifying which category branches to test (e.g., c("GO:CC", "GO:BP", "GO:MF") or "KEGG") ;; gene2cat=A data frame or list mapping genes to categories for custom/non-native category tests ;; use_genes_without_cat=Flag to switch between counting or ignoring genes with no category annotations in the background set
- alternatives: Hypergeometric distribution (method="Hypergeometric") which ignores length bias and is only appropriate for data without selection bias (like microarrays) ;; Random sampling (method="Sampling") which generates the true null distribution but is computationally expensive and requires a very high repcnt to accurately call enrichment for rare terms compared to the default Wallenius approximation
- when_to_use: When performing functional enrichment analysis (GO, KEGG, or custom categories) on RNA-seq data where gene length or read count bias confounds the probability of a gene being called differentially expressed
- pitfalls: Ignoring length bias (using standard hypergeometric tests) can lead to false positives/negatives because longer genes are more likely to be called DE ;; Using method="Sampling" with too few replicates (repcnt) will fail to accurately calculate very low p-values, potentially missing significantly enriched terms after multiple testing correction ;; Using org.Hs.egGO instead of org.Hs.egGO2ALLEGS when manually extracting GO mappings, as the former misses links to genes arising from child GO categories ;; If the genome/ID combination is not in the local database (geneLenDataBase), gene lengths must be manually specified or fetched from TxDb/UCSC

workflows.name: standard_go_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform GO enrichment analysis on RNA-seq DE genes while correcting for gene length bias using the default Wallenius approximation.
input: assayed.genes (character vector of all genes assayed)
de.genes (character vector of differentially expressed genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Format gene vector ;; 2. Fit the Probability Weighting Function (PWF) using nullp ;; 3. Run GO enrichment analysis using goseq ;; 4. Extract and interpret enriched categories using GO.db
workflows.code:
gene.vector <- as.integer(assayed.genes %in% de.genes)
names(gene.vector) <- assayed.genes
pwf <- nullp(genes, "hg19", "ensGene")
GO.wall <- goseq(pwf, "hg19", "ensGene")
enriched.GO <- GO.wall$category[p.adjust(GO.wall$over_represented_pvalue,
  method = "BH"
) < .05]
library(GO.db)
for (go in enriched.GO[1:10]) {
  print(GOTERM[[go]])
  cat("--------------------------------------\n")
}

workflows.name: custom_category_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform enrichment analysis using custom gene-to-category mappings (like KEGG pathways) or non-native organisms.
input: genes (named binary vector of assayed genes and DE status)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct custom gene-to-category mapping list ;; 2. Fit the PWF using nullp ;; 3. Run enrichment analysis using goseq with the gene2cat argument
workflows.code:
en2eg <- as.list(org.Hs.egENSEMBL2EG)
eg2kegg <- as.list(org.Hs.egPATH)
grepKEGG <- function(id, mapkeys) {
  unique(unlist(mapkeys[id], use.names = FALSE))
}
kegg <- lapply(en2eg, grepKEGG, eg2kegg)
pwf <- nullp(genes, "hg19", "ensGene")
KEGG <- goseq(pwf, gene2cat = kegg)

workflows.name: count_bias_corrected_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform enrichment analysis correcting for read count bias instead of gene length bias.
input: genes (named binary vector of assayed genes and DE status)
counts (matrix of raw read counts per gene)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate read count bias per gene ;; 2. Fit the PWF using nullp with custom bias.data ;; 3. Run GO enrichment analysis using goseq
workflows.code:
countbias <- rowSums(counts)[rowSums(counts) != 0]
pwf.counts <- nullp(genes, bias.data = countbias)
GO.counts <- goseq(pwf.counts, "hg19", "ensGene")
